clue.text: Taking part in an oral examination

definitions.text: Taking part in an oral examination

parts.words: Taking part in an oral examination
parts.note: read as sampling food or wine in the mouth to judge it, not sitting a spoken viva at a university

explanation.surface: A student is busy sitting a viva voce exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a spoken test; the examination is really done with the mouth and palate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampling food or drink means judging it with the mouth, a literal oral examination.

clue.text: Bar drunken tramp pinching pair of spectacles

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so one piece is held inside the other
a drunk staggers about, so these letters reel into a new order

parts.note: two round lenses look like the letters O O

explanation.surface: A drunk vagrant in a pub steals someone's glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of spectacles' is a picture: two round lenses look like two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the bar of a pub or inn where drinks are served.

clue.text: Winning first prize for dredging pond

definitions.meaning: to win the whole pot or every prize on offer, an idiom from betting
literally ladling out water or mud from a pool

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking all the winnings, and literally means emptying a pool with a scoop.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to smooth clothes with a heated appliance
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes is ironing them, and an iron is a type of golf club.

clue.text: Lucky thing in well-paid employment

definitions.meaning: an exclamation meaning it was fortunate that something happened
a desirable position with good pay

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an exclamation of relief at good fortune and a description of a fine position.

clue.text: Impact family made on one from the country

parts.note: a bump is a knock or impact
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Something that hit a family affected a person from the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an unsophisticated rustic, someone from rural parts.

clue.text: Herbert Ramsay's middle name?

indicators.note: the middle of the two names is taken, the run of letters straddling them

explanation.surface: A question asking what a man called Herbert Ramsay has as his second given name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle name' looks like the definition, but only 'name' defines; 'middle' points to the letters at the centre of Herbert Ramsay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertram is a man's given name.

clue.text: Keep channel circumventing it

parts.note: a keep is the central tower of a castle, and this is the water-filled ditch running round it

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay on one TV channel while avoiding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun for a castle's stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-filled defensive ditch surrounds a castle, encircling its keep.

clue.text: How sir gains advancement on board?

definitions.text: How sir gains advancement on board?

parts.words: How sir gains advancement on board?
parts.note: a titled man advancing on a company board, read instead as a chess piece moving across the board

explanation.surface: Asks how a titled man gets promoted on a company's board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a boardroom, but it is the chessboard where the horse-headed piece moves.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece called a knight advances on the chessboard in an L-shaped path.

clue.text: Candidate found there was no motorway in Spain repeatedly

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for Spain is given more than once, so it appears twice

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A candidate discovered there was no motorway in Spain, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward as a candidate for a post or award.

clue.text: Picture book theory used by the press

parts.note: a photo is a picture
a journal is a book of records or a diary
an ism is a doctrine or theory

explanation.surface: A picture book about a theory employed by newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: News reporting through photographs is a practice used by newspapers and magazines.

clue.text: Sorry, nothing works!

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
ops is short for opuses, musical works

explanation.surface: An apology because none of the equipment functions.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation acknowledging a small mistake, like a quick apology.

clue.text: Rocky inlet just starting to enter crossing-place

indicators.note: one piece enters another, going inside it

parts.note: a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

indicators.note: the start of the word just, its first letter

explanation.surface: A stony inlet is about to reach a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just starting' gives J, which goes into FORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A fjord is a long narrow sea inlet between steep cliffs, typical of Norway.

clue.text: Be successful going round Hungary for gorse

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to win is to be successful
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: Advice to succeed by travelling around Hungary to find gorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Whin is a dialect name for the prickly shrub gorse, also called furze.

clue.text: Did not finish writing certificate

indicators.note: the word is left incomplete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: script is handwriting or written text

explanation.surface: Someone failed to complete writing out a certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did not finish' cuts the final T from SCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrip is a certificate entitling the holder to shares or money.

clue.text: Not starting to be spiteful when needing to scratch

indicators.note: the word loses its start, so its first letter goes

parts.note: bitchy means spiteful or malicious

explanation.surface: Someone stops being nasty when they get an itch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not starting' removes the B from BITCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling an irritation on the skin makes one want to scratch.

clue.text: Only small compartment for its driver

definitions.text: Only small compartment for its driver

parts.note: mini means small, as in a miniskirt
a cab is the enclosed part of a vehicle where the driver sits

explanation.surface: Complains that the driver gets only a tiny space.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a small taxi and also builds it; 'Only' is a link adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A small private hire taxi booked by phone rather than hailed in the street.

clue.text: Steam is bothering painter

indicators.note: being bothered unsettles things, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Steam from something is troubling an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothering' rearranges STEAM IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist, a leader of Fauvism.

clue.text: Musical minimum?

parts.note: a string on a violin named by a note, also a skimpy garment covering the bare minimum

explanation.surface: A question about the least amount of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The string tuned to a particular note is also the name of a very scanty undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin's lowest string, sharing its name with a tiny piece of underwear.

clue.text: Gags owl fluttering over large built-up area

indicators.note: a bird flapping its wings moves about, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A gagged owl flapping its wings over a sprawling city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges GAGS OWL; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, a big urban area.

clue.text: Encouraging Hamish to take in fabric

indicators.note: the words take the answer inside them, holding it within

explanation.surface: Urging a Scotsman named Hamish to alter some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' sounds like dressmaking, but it points to the letters inside Encouraging Hamish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a cotton cloth woven in checks.

clue.text: Round permutation of ciphers

indicators.note: a permutation is a reordering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complete cycle of rearranging coded messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'permutation of' rearranges CIPHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like a ball, so round in form.

clue.text: Substitute's never-ending status

indicators.note: the word has no ending, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: standing is one's status or rank

explanation.surface: A replacement player's position never comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' cuts the G from STANDING; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in replaces someone temporarily, a substitute.

clue.text: Charlie had red sort of cheese

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a sort of something is a version of it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie had a red-rinded cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' does double duty in the surface, suggesting a kind of cheese, but it is the anagram signal for HAD RED, giving HEDDAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard English cheese named after a Somerset village.

clue.text: Wean off afresh

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Weaning a child off the breast once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something anew is to do it again, from the start.

clue.text: Work for one's bread

parts.note: earning a living, read instead as working dough with the hands

explanation.surface: Doing a job to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work for one's bread' sounds like earning one's keep but means pummelling dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is pressed and folded by hand before baking a loaf.

clue.text: Wow, there's zero first on the curve

indicators.note: the zero is placed first, before the other piece

parts.note: O is the figure zero
gee is an exclamation like wow

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at nothing being placed at the start of a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is an S-shaped curve or moulding in architecture.

clue.text: Are endlessly surrounding footballers from a distance

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it
the word has no end, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.surface: Players are always encircled when seen from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests players encircled; FA, the Football Association, stands for footballers in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or from a great distance.

clue.text: Protein coming from Zambia, East Indies and Norway

parts.note: Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia
EI is the abbreviation for East Indies
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A protein sourced from three far-flung places.
explanation.definitionFit: Zein is a protein found in maize.

clue.text: Get mad and take a dive

definitions.meaning: literally plunge into the deepest part of a swimming pool

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for losing one's temper comes from jumping into the deepest part of a swimming pool.

clue.text: Two beasts revealing rare metal

parts.note: a wolf is a wild beast
a ram is a male sheep, another beast

explanation.surface: Two animals uncover a scarce metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two beasts' gives two animals; 'revealing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a rare metallic element.

clue.text: Failure to exercise a right by nurse on shift

indicators.note: to shift is to move about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse on her work shift fails to exercise her rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a nurse's working hours but rearranges NURSE ON; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, nonuser is the neglect to use a right, which may cause it to lapse.
